title: Algebraic cohomology and the Dolbeault derivative
statement: Let $X$ be a smooth projective scheme over $\mathbf C$ [def-pc-scheme], [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], [def-pc-projective-morphism]. Its analytification $M=X^{\mathrm{an}}$ (the space of complex points with its analytic topology and holomorphic charts) is a finite disjoint union of compact Kähler manifolds; dimensions may differ between components. A Kähler metric means a Hermitian metric whose associated real $(1,1)$-form is closed, and on $M$ one may use the restriction of the Fubini--Study metric from a projective embedding. Write $A^{p,q}(M)$ for the complex vector space of smooth complex differential forms of type $(p,q)$, with $d_{\mathrm{an}}=\partial+\bar\partial$, and put $H^{p,q}_{\bar\partial}(M)=\ker(\bar\partial:A^{p,q}\to A^{p,q+1})/\operatorname{im}(\bar\partial:A^{p,q-1}\to A^{p,q})$, with negative-degree spaces zero. Let $\Omega^1_{X/\mathbf C}$ be the sheaf obtained by gluing Kähler differential modules [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], let $\Omega^0=\mathcal O_X$, and let $d_X:\mathcal O_X\to\Omega^1_{X/\mathbf C}$ be the universal $\mathbf C$-linear derivation. There are canonical $\mathbf C$-linear isomorphisms $c_{p,q}:H^q(X,\Omega^p_{X/\mathbf C})\cong H^{p,q}_{\bar\partial}(M)$ for $p=0,1$ and all $q\geq0$. The algebraic cohomology here is right-derived global sections in Zariski sheaves of $\mathbf C$-vector spaces, canonically agreeing with module cohomology [pqf-def-cohomology]. For every $a\in H^q(X,\mathcal O_X)$ and every $\bar\partial$-closed $\alpha\in A^{0,q}(M)$ representing $c_{0,q}(a)$, one has $c_{1,q}(H^q(X,d_X)(a))=[(-1)^q\partial\alpha]$, using the Dolbeault resolution with differential $\bar\partial$ and its chain map $(-1)^q\partial$ in resolution degree $q$.

source.place: WANTED locally: Popa, proof of Theorem 1.6.6, printed pp.26--27, algebraic cohomology identified with forms of types (0,j) and (1,j). Read online https://people.math.harvard.edu/~mpopa/271/Kodaira-posted.pdf. The comparison here makes explicit the GAGA and Dolbeault compatibility used there.

proof.text: By [lem-pc-projective-proper] $X\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf C$ is proper, hence separated and of finite type [def-weil-proper-morphism]. $\mathbf P^N_{\mathbf C}=\mathbf P(\{0,\dots,N\};\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf C)$ [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change] is proper by [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper]; it is smooth, since its standard opens $D_+(T_j)$ of [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-twisting-sheaf-charts], base changed to $\mathbf C$, are affine spaces $\mathbf A^N_{\mathbf C}$, smooth by [sbc-lem-affine-space-smooth], and smoothness is local on the source [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-local-on-source]. Hence [lem-sfb-smooth-analytification-cotangent] applies to the closed immersion $X\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^N_{\mathbf C}$ given by projectivity and makes $M$ a closed complex submanifold of $\mathbf P^N(\mathbf C)$. The latter is compact as the continuous quotient of the unit sphere in $\mathbf C^{N+1}$, hence $M$ is compact. Its connected components are open (use connected coordinate balls), so compactness gives finitely many, each compact. On an affine projective chart restrict the Fubini--Study form $\omega=i\partial\bar\partial\log(1+\lVert z\rVert^2)$. Its Hermitian quadratic form, up to a positive constant, is $((1+\lVert z\rVert^2)\lVert v\rVert^2-|\langle z,v\rangle|^2)/(1+\lVert z\rVert^2)^2>0$ for $v\ne0$ by Cauchy--Schwarz. The local potentials differ on overlaps by the logarithm of the squared norm of an invertible holomorphic transition function, whose $\partial\bar\partial$ is zero. Thus these forms glue. The differential identities of [lem-sfb-dolbeault-acyclic-resolution] give $d\omega=0$. Restriction to each holomorphic tangent subspace preserves positivity and closedness. This constructs the stated Kähler metric, also when dimensions differ.

proof.text: Let $F_0=\mathcal O_X,F_1=\Omega^1_{X/\mathbf C}$. The structure sheaf has rank one, and [lem-ag-smooth-relative-differentials-finite-locally-free] says that $F_1$ is finite locally free, without constant rank. Apply [lem-sfb-gaga-derived-coherent-sections] to both. The isomorphisms of [lem-sfb-smooth-analytification-cotangent] identify their analytic sheaves with $\Omega_M^p$, $p=0,1$. By [lem-pe-ringed-site-derived-evaluation-slice], applied on the sites of opens with ring sheaf $\mathcal O_X$ and then with the constant ring sheaf $\mathbf C$, both cohomology conventions identify canonically with underlying abelian sheaf cohomology. Naturality in multiplication by every $\lambda\in\mathbf C$ makes these identifications complex-linear. The enough-injectives hypothesis holds by [lem-sc-ringed-space-module-sheaves-enough-injectives], for each of these ringed spaces. This justifies the module-cohomology convention in the statement without interpreting $d_X$ as O-linear.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 1.6.6, printed pp.26--27; agent expansion of its GAGA--Dolbeault input

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-dolbeault-acyclic-resolution] the complexes $\mathcal A_M^{p,\bullet}$ with differential $\bar\partial$ are bounded-below global-section-acyclic resolutions of $\Omega_M^p$. Apply [lem-sfb-ringed-acyclic-resolution-derived-maps] with the identity morphism of the constant-$\mathbf C$ ringed topos of $M$; enough injectives follows from [lem-sc-ringed-space-module-sheaves-enough-injectives]. It supplies the canonical derived-resolution isomorphism $Q\Gamma(M,\mathcal A_M^{p,\bullet})\cong R\Gamma(M,\Omega_M^p[0])$. Compose its inverse with $g_{F_p}$ and the analytic sheaf identification from step 2. Apply the functor $H^q$ to this composite derived isomorphism; by the definition of complex cohomology its target is precisely the kernel/image quotient $H^{p,q}_{\bar\partial}(M)$. Here $g_{F_p}$ is read in $D^+(\operatorname{Ab})$ through the exact forgetful functor; both derived sections are computed from injective resolutions in sheaves of $\mathbf C$-vector spaces. For $\lambda\in\mathbf C$, multiplication by $\lambda$ on $\Omega_M^p$ and on $\mathcal A_M^{p,\bullet}$ is an augmentation-preserving map of resolutions, so the identity-morphism case of [lem-sfb-ringed-acyclic-resolution-derived-maps] makes the resolution comparison commute with it; $g_{F_p}$ is $\mathbf C$-linear, being a morphism of $D^+(\operatorname{Vect}_{\mathbf C})$. Hence $H^q$ of the composite is $\mathbf C$-linear. Define $c_{p,q}$ to be this map. Thus the comparison is constructed before taking degrees, rather than by choosing individual vector-space isomorphisms.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 1.6.6, printed pp.26--27; agent expansion of its GAGA--Dolbeault input

proof.text: Write $j_p:F_p\to\pi_*\Omega_M^p$ for the coefficient maps underlying the GAGA arrows after the cotangent identification. The last formula of [lem-sfb-smooth-analytification-cotangent] gives the equality of complex-linear sheaf maps $j_1d_X=\pi_*(d_{\mathrm{hol}})j_0$, checked on every local regular function. Consequently the two maps $F_0[0]\to R\pi_*\Omega_M^1[0]$ agree: each is induced by that same coefficient map followed by the natural map from direct to derived pushforward. Applying $R\Gamma$ gives $g_{F_1}R\Gamma(d_X)=R\Gamma(d_{\mathrm{hol}})g_{F_0}$. This uses the actual coefficient maps defining $g$, not a claim that analytification is functorial on non-O-linear maps.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 1.6.6, printed pp.26--27; agent expansion of its GAGA--Dolbeault input

proof.text: Set $T^r=(-1)^r\partial:\mathcal A_M^{0,r}\to\mathcal A_M^{1,r}$. By [lem-sfb-dolbeault-acyclic-resolution], $\bar\partial T^r=(-1)^{r+1}\partial\bar\partial=T^{r+1}\bar\partial$, so $T$ is a complex-linear chain map. In degree zero it extends $d_{\mathrm{hol}}$ on the holomorphic-function augmentations. The identity-morphism case of [lem-sfb-ringed-acyclic-resolution-derived-maps] therefore identifies $Q\Gamma(T)$ with $R\Gamma(d_{\mathrm{hol}})$ under the derived comparisons used to define $c$. Taking $H^q$ in this equality and in step 4 yields $c_{1,q}H^q(d_X)=[T^q]c_{0,q}$. For any closed representative $\alpha$ this is exactly $[(-1)^q\partial\alpha]$. A change $\alpha\mapsto\alpha+\bar\partial\beta$ changes the output by $\bar\partial((-1)^{q+1}\partial\beta)$, so the formula holds for every representative. For $q=0$ the negative-degree space is zero, and for empty $M$ all the spaces vanish.

The statement is true, unchanged and as the parent uses it. The sign (-1)^q is forced, because plain ∂ anticommutes with ∂̄ and is not a chain map. Small cases checked: empty, P^1, elliptic curve, q=0, q>dim. Fubini-Study: positivity, overlap gluing and dω=0 checked. Step-4 sheaf square j_1 d_X = π_*(d_hol) j_0 and the step-5 identity-case resolution naturality checked; the result is independent of the representative. Two repairs plus one clarification. (1) C1, step 1: it applied the analytification node to X ↪ P^N_C without showing that X and P^N_C are separated, finite type and smooth. I added lem-pc-projective-proper, def-weil-proper-morphism, lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper, def-nagata-projective-space-base-change, lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-twisting-sheaf-charts, sbc-lem-affine-space-smooth and lem-weil-pbc-smooth-local-on-source, set the step to elementary=false, and declared the four off-route tools in split_report.tool_uses. (2) E5, step 3: it composed a D^+(Ab) resolution comparison with g_F in D^+(Vect_C) and never justified the asserted C-linearity of c_{p,q}. I added the forgetful-functor reading, plus scalar naturality from the identity case of lem-sfb-ringed-acyclic-resolution-derived-maps. (3) Clarification: the cotangent node now states that (O_X)^an ≅ O_M is h⊗f ↦ h f^an, which step 4 needs. lem-pe-ringed-site-derived-evaluation-slice is on route because the unit uses sk-prop-sf-comparison; the declared tool uses for lem-ag-smooth-relative-differentials-finite-locally-free and lem-sc-ringed-space-module-sheaves-enough-injectives are accepted.
